excerpt: Figure 2 describes a visual spatial attention task with central arrow cues, a 1 s cue-target interval, and difficult orientation or motion judgments at the cued location. The alpha-band TSE waveforms showed a sustained divergence beginning at roughly 500 ms, with amplitudes larger over occipital cortex ipsilateral to the attended direction.
overview: The spatial result links alpha topography to the location of likely distracters. Since only the cued location was task-relevant, the ipsilateral occipital alpha increase is evidence that alpha targets the cortical representation of the ignored hemifield rather than merely tracking general alertness or motor preparation.
title: Retinotopic Spatial Alpha Bias
